itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad, airport transfer and trek briefing
Day 3: Drive to Askoli from Skardu (3,044m)
Day 4: Glacier trek begins toward Jhola
Day 6: Trek to Khobusre / glacier section
Day 7: Urdukas, shorter day for acclimatization
Day 10: K2 Base Camp (5,150m), flexible scheduling
Day 11: Begin return journey toward Skardu
pros: Local Gilgit-Baltistan company (License DTS-GB-046); guides from Balti communities
Government trekking permit fees explicitly included in price
Domestic flights, all transfers, accommodation and all meals bundled in
Satellite phone for emergencies provided
Transparent tiered pricing for both international and Pakistani nationals
cons: Porter weight limit only 14kg, lowest among these operators
Just one soft acclimatization day (shorter Urdukas day), no full rest day
Solo price is steep ($4,200) versus group rates
Insurance, personal gear and tips all excluded
verdict: Best for budget-conscious and group trekkers who want a genuine locally-owned Balti operator with permits included; the per-person price drops sharply with group size.
excludes: Travel insurance, international airfare, personal equipment, extra Islamabad nights, tips/gratuities, and force-majeure costs.

itinerary: Day 3: Sightseeing and preparation day in Skardu
Day 4: Drive to Askole, trek start
Day 7: Trek stage on Baltoro Glacier
Day 8: Acclimatization and rest day at Urdukas
Day 16: Return trek stage to Askole
pros: Skardu-based local operator with claimed 40 years of operation
Generous 20kg porter weight allowance per traveller
Small groups capped at twelve people
Dedicated full rest/acclimatization day at Urdukas (Day 8)
Low fully-refundable deposit ($170)
cons: Royalty fees and CKNP (Central Karakoram National Park) fees collected SEPARATELY, not in package
Excess-baggage penalties ($100-110 per extra 5kg)
Wide price spread ($1,790-$3,900) makes true cost season-dependent
Travel insurance not included
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting a long, well-paced 20-day local-operator trip with a real rest day and small groups; just budget separately for royalty/park fees.
excludes: Royalty fees and CKNP park fees (separate), travel insurance, excess porter weight over 20kg.

itinerary: Day 3: Fly to Skardu, acclimatization activities
Day 4: Drive by jeep to Askole, trek start
Day 7: Rest day in Paju (porters bake bread)
Day 12: Trek toward K2 Base Camp
Day 13: K2 Base Camp (4,980m) and back to Concordia
pros: Trekking permit and environmental fee included
Helicopter rescue deposits and satellite phones provided
Clear tiered group pricing ($2,195-$2,400/person)
Dedicated rest day at Paju (Day 7)
English-speaking guides, AC coaches, domestic flights bundled
cons: Nepal-based operator (Tarakeshwar, Nepal), not Pakistan-local
Porter allowance 15kg; extra porters cost $175
Medical/evacuation and helicopter rescue fees themselves excluded
Single supplement +$200; early hotel check-in extra
verdict: Best for value-seekers comfortable with a Nepal-based operator running a Pakistan trek; competitive group pricing with permit and environmental fees included.
excludes: International airfare, visas, medications/first aid, ground evacuation and helicopter rescue fees, extra porters, tips.

itinerary: Day 5-6: Trekking to Jula and Paju Camp
Day 7: Acclimatization and rest day at Paju
Day 12: Trek to Broad Peak BC and K2 Base Camp (Gilkey Memorial)
Day 14: Trek to Goro 1 / Biango Camp
pros: Skardu-based local operator with licensed Balti guides
Trekking permit, waste-management fee and toll/bridge charges included
Both a rest day at Skardu (Day 3) and acclimatization day at Paju (Day 7)
Tiered private/group pricing ($2,300-$4,500) with auto-applied discounts
Two summits in one day (Broad Peak BC + K2 BC) and contingency day built in
cons: Porter weight limit 15kg per trekker
Personal insurance, visa fees and international flights excluded
Personal climbing equipment only arranged on request (extra cost)
Inclusions/exclusions lists overlap confusingly on the page
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting a local Skardu operator with strong acclimatization built in and transparent group-discount pricing including permit/waste fees.
excludes: Personal insurance, visa and fees, international flights, personal clothing/equipment, extra hotel stays, tips, miscellaneous.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad and orientation
Day 3: Flight to Skardu (or road via Chilas), acclimatization day
Day 7: Free day at Paiyu, porters prepare food
Day 12: K2 Base Camp (5,135m) and return to Concordia
pros: Local Pakistani operator (Licence 396), claimed 29 years of experience
Trekking permits included in package
Free acclimatization/exploration day at Paiyu (Day 7)
Steady, leisurely pacing (~5-7 hrs/day on most trek days)
Private/tailor-made option available alongside set group departures
cons: Porter allowance 15kg per person
Sleeping bag NOT included (personal item)
Group price from $2,620 is higher than some local peers
Tips, meals in Islamabad and personal expenses excluded
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting an experienced, established local Pakistani operator with a gentle pace and the flexibility of private or group departures.
excludes: International airfare, visas, meals in Islamabad, sleeping bag, personal expenses (phone/liquor/soft drinks), tips for drivers/porters/staff.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad (540m), transfer to hotel
Day 2: Fly to Skardu (2,228m), transfer to hotel
Day 3: Trek briefing, permits, gear check and shopping
Day 9: Trek to Goro II (4,300m), 6-7 hours
Day 10: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp (4,800m)
Day 11: Trek to K2 Base Camp (5,150m)
pros: Permits for K2 Base Camp Trek included
Generous 1:1 porter ratio (one porter per member)
Dedicated rest/acclimatization day (Day 7 at Paiyu)
Three meals a day and certified trekking guide included
Finisher K2 Base Camp trekking certificate provided
cons: Highest starting price among local-style operators ($3,900)
Mandatory rescue insurance (min USD $25,000 coverage) excluded
Tips required at minimum 10% of total per member
Headquarters base (Nepal vs Pakistan) not clearly stated on page
verdict: Best for trekkers prioritizing a 1:1 porter ratio and a formal, certificate-backed itinerary, who don't mind a premium price and the operator's ambiguous home base.
excludes: Pakistan visa fee, medical/emergency rescue insurance (min $25,000), personal gear, tips (min 10% of total per member).

itinerary: Day 3: Flight to Skardu, market and prep day
Day 4: Drive to Askole, trek start
Day 12: K2 Base Camp and return to Concordia
Day 13: Trek stage toward Gondogoro La
Day 18: Trek to Hushe, drive to Skardu
pros: Western plus local guides; US 4-season alpine tents supplied
Generous 20kg porter allowance per person
Two rest days built in (Urdukas Day 9, Concordia Day 14)
Spectacular Gondogoro La loop exit (5,650m) rather than out-and-back
Charging generator provided; experienced founder (21 Pakistan trips since 2018)
cons: Foreign (US-founded) operator at premium price ($4,490-$5,330)
Mandatory Global Rescue membership / travel insurance excluded
Porter services over 20kg cost extra; single tent supplement extra
Extra hotel nights from delays not covered
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting a Western-guided, comfortable expedition with the dramatic Gondogoro La crossing and two acclimatization days, at a premium price.
excludes: International flights, travel insurance (mandatory Global Rescue), tips, porter weight over 20kg, single-tent supplement, delay-related hotel nights.

itinerary: Day 4: Jeep and trek to Jhola
Day 10: Trek to K2 Base Camp
Day 11: Second night at K2 Base Camp
Day 12: Begin return / toward Gondogoro La
Day 17: Contingency / rest day to Hushe
pros: Two nights sleeping at K2 Base Camp for strong acclimatization
Gondogoro La crossing (5,585m) as a high-pass exit route
Contingency/rest day (Day 17) built into schedule
Small max group size of 10
Employs local Pakistani staff under an established Western brand
cons: Highest price here at USD $5,750 per person
Foreign-based (Vail, Colorado, USA), not a local operator
Page does NOT list what is included in the price
No exclusions section: permit fees, porter weight limits and extras unstated
verdict: Best for trekkers who value a well-known Western brand, small groups and two nights at base camp, and who will ask directly for the inclusion/exclusion detail the page omits.
excludes: Not published on the page; no inclusions or exclusions section is provided, so permit fees, porter limits and extra costs are unstated.

itinerary: Day 6: Drive by jeep to Askole farming village
Day 14: Walk to Broad Peak Base Camp
Day 18: Trek down valley to Hushe village
pros: All permit fees included in price
Full base camp setup with dining tents, showers and bathroom
Reserve weather days built in (Days 24-25) plus a rest day at Paiyu
Gondogoro La crossing (5,585m) for a scenic exit
Experienced expedition organizer (Dan Mazur) with local Balti agent
cons: Foreign-organized (British/American), not a local operator
Premium single price $5,850 with no group discount tiers shown
Travel/rescue insurance and Pakistan visa excluded
Single tent only via paid upgrade
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting the most generous schedule (25 days with reserve weather days), full base-camp comforts and an experienced Western expedition organizer, at a premium flat price.
excludes: International flights, trekking rescue and travel insurance, personal climbing/trekking equipment, Pakistan visa.
